subject: Urgent: Skyline production latency spike — KV cache harmonics causing HOL blocking
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@skyline.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@skyline.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production alerts — sudden p99 spike and errors (Skyline Prod)

Jonas —

We started seeing a sharp p99 latency jump around 08:50 PT and a subsequent increase in 500/502 errors. Throughput for our write-heavy endpoints dropped by ~40% as requests queue up. Our SRE pulled a few traces and there are repeated waits on call to /kv/get for tenant skyline-* keys. Attaching a small log excerpt and a heap snapshot (attached) — hope this helps.

Key numbers (last 30m):
- p50: 120ms -> unchanged
- p95: 420ms -> unchanged
- p99: 1.8s -> 4.7s
- error rate (5m): 0.3% -> 3.5%
- RPS: 200 -> 120

We are live in us-west-2. Can you advise immediate mitigation? If this requires an internal config change we need a clear rollback plan.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of SRE, Skyline.ai
Attachments: skyline_logs_excerpt.txt (text), heapdump-20290314.tar.gz (tgz)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@skyline.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:20:18 -0700
Subject: Re: production alerts — sudden p99 spike and errors (Skyline Prod)

Aisha — thanks for the quick heads up and logs. We're treating this as P1. Hannah and Marcus are on the first-pass triage.

Immediate asks: can you confirm whether Skyline traffic is primarily short-prefix queries (many similar keys) right now? Any sudden campaign or batch job that started ~08:40-08:55 PT? That helps us validate possible hot-key / HOL blocking vectors.

Planned immediate mitigations (we'll confirm before applying):
- Disable prefix prefetch for Skyline tenant on the routing layer (safe rollback).
- Reduce batch window on the serving side for tenant-affine lanes from 8ms -> 2ms to drop HOL risk.
- Temporarily increase KV TTL/occupancy for skyline-* to prevent aggressive eviction thrash.

I'm opening a bridge for 11:00 PT and will include an exec summary for your leadership. Attaching our initial checklist.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: incident_checklist.md

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:35:05 -0700
Subject: Action: KV cache harmonics (Skyline) — priority P1

Team — Skyline reporting p99 spike + throughput collapse. Quick summary from customer logs: repeated long waits for /kv/get on skyline-* keys and high eviction churn. Hypothesis: a small set of tenant prefixes are triggering continuous prefetch and eviction cycles that starve hot lanes (HOL blocking) and cascade to increased latency and dropped throughput.

What we see in tenant data:
- High prefix similarity (same 6 prefixes account for ~65% of lookups)
- KV eviction rate jumped 9x at ~08:50 PT coincident with batch job start at Skyline (customer confirmed).
- Serving runtime shows long synchronous waits in the prefix prefetch path for those tenant lanes.

Immediate plan (0–30m):
1) Disable prefix prefetch toggles for skyline tenant (safe toggle; rollback -> re-enable).
2) Lower batching window for affected pools (8ms -> 2ms) targeted to tenant lanes only.
3) Increase local KV TTL/occupancy cap for skyline to reduce churn.
4) Spin up 20% additional capacity in the skyline lane pool to absorb in-flight requests (non-disruptive).
5) Prepare fallback: pin requests to a smaller, non-prefetching model variant if latency persists.

Owners: Hannah -> toggles + quick validity checks; Marcus -> batch config + capacity; Laura -> exec communications and customer liaison. I'll join the 11:00 bridge.

References: runbook-prefetch.pdf (attached), https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2148

— Jonas

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:55:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Action: KV cache harmonics (Skyline) — priority P1

Quick update — triage findings and actions taken: 
- Observed HOL blocking on 3 hot shards pinned to skyline prefix group "skl-rl-6".
- Disabled prefix prefetch for skyline across us-west-2 (rolling toggle to avoid cache stampede).
- Increased KV TTL from 30s -> 120s for skyline tenant.
- Deployed batch window reduction (8ms->2ms) to target serving pools for skyline.
- Launched +20% capacity on affected pools; warm-up in progress.

Early signal: p99 dropped from ~4.7s -> ~1.1s within 7 minutes of toggles; error rate trending down. We're monitoring for re-eviction waves.

Next steps: keep toggles for 60 minutes, then gradually re-enable prefetch with tighter limits and per-prefix backoff. Marcus - coordinate the ramp plan; I'll capture a short RCA once stable.

— Hannah

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@skyline.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 10:05:44 -0700
Subject: Re: production alerts — sudden p99 spike and errors (Skyline Prod)

Aisha — short update for your leadership and ops: we've identified a prefetch/eviction interaction that produced HOL blocking on a small set of skyline prefixes coincident with a Skyline batch job. Actions we took immediately:
- Disabled prefix prefetch for the Skyline tenant in us-west-2 (rollback available).
- Reduced batching window for skyline-affine serving pools from 8ms -> 2ms.
- Increased KV TTL/occupancy to reduce eviction churn.
- Brought +20% temporary capacity online for affected lanes.

Metrics so far (10:03 PT): p99 dropped to ~1.1s, error rate down to 0.6%, RPS recovering. We're keeping the toggles for 60 minutes and plan a controlled re-enable with per-prefix backoff.

We'll host an incident bridge at 11:00 PT to review root causes and the safe re-enable plan. I'll include Laura (cc) for executive touchpoints. Please share any other traces or a concise timeline of Skyline-side jobs that started around 08:40-09:00 PT — that will help finalize the RCA.

Attachments: kv_snapshot_20290314.json, runbook-prefetch.pdf

— Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(jo.nas@redwood.ai)

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@skyline.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@skyline.ai>, Skyline SRE <sre@skyline.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 11:40:02 -0700
Subject: Re: production alerts — sudden p99 spike and errors (Skyline Prod)

Jonas / team — thanks for the fast response and clear mitigation. After the toggles and capacity bump we saw the p99 fall back to baseline and errors subside. We confirmed the batch job that triggered the pattern was an internal nightly indexing job (started 08:46 PT). We'll throttle that job and follow the re-enable playbook you shared.

Appreciate the thorough communication and the exec-level visibility — Laura, thanks for being on the call. We'll follow up with a timeline and any additional traces.

Aisha Patel
Head of SRE, Skyline.ai
